title: Reservation Reconciliation Orchestrator and Noise Detector Prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: After the Feb 2025 capacity incident where multiple tenants triggered eviction storms and tail-latency regressions, we need a small orchestration service to reconcile per-tenant reservations against live telemetry and an automated noisy-tenant detector that can trigger isolation actions and soft reservation changes. This ticket tracks the prototype implementation and staged rollout of a Reservation Reconciliation Orchestrator (RRO) plus a Noise Detector Runner (NDR). Goals: 1) reduce incident blast radius by surfacing and automatically soft-resizing mis-sized reservations; 2) provide a fast, reversible isolation action for noisy tenants prior to hard evictions; 3) integrate with existing burst controls so we avoid oscillation; 4) ship a minimal safe canary path that ops can opt into and out of without redeploying runtime agents.
acceptance_criteria: RRO reads aggregated per-tenant telemetry (token_use_rate, median latency, 95th latency, eviction_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio) and computes a suggested reservation delta within safety bounds
NDR emits a noisy-tenant signal when tenant metrics exceed configured thresholds for sustained windows (configurable: 3m/10m/30m) and records the reason code
Implemented a burst-governor shim that can accept 'soft_limit' adjustments from the RRO and enforces a decaying token-window on burst consumption
A /ops UI panel renders recommendations and allows manual approve/reject; automated actions require opt-in flag and explicit SLA guardrails
Canary rollout to 5 dedicated GPU pools with synthetic tenants shows no more than 5% change in baseline throughput and no increase in SLO misses over 72h
Unit and e2e tests for reconciliation algorithm plus chaos test harness that simulates a noisy tenant and verifies isolation path
proposed_solution: Architectural sketch: a lightweight orchestrator (k8s Cron + controller) polls sanitized telemetry from metrics pipeline (prometheus pushgateway -> aggregator) and runs a reconciliation loop. The reconciler computes a confidence-weighted reservation delta using recent load, KV cache leverage, and historical reservation utilization. If confidence > 0.8 and action is idempotent, the reconciler writes a candidate change to the decisions-log (immutable) and to a staging API. The Noise Detector Runner is a separate worker that applies rules (percentile thresholds + spike detection) to flag tenants and optionally apply a transient isolation (cgroup v2 soft quota + burst token decay). We prefer soft, reversible actions over hard evictions. The burst-governor uses a leaky-bucket with configurable decay and a backoff multiplier on repeated triggers. All actions are auditable and tied to an ops approval flow by default; automated mode requires explicit entitlement. Key integration points: reservations service API, tenant-metadata service, RBAC audit logs, console/ops dashboard, and alerting on false-positive rate.
design_decisions: Choice: external orchestrator vs in-runtime autoscaler — external allows faster ops control and less runtime churn; downside is eventual consistency which we mitigate via decision logs and idempotency
Noise detection approach: percentile + sustained window preferred to single-sample anomalies to reduce FP rate
Soft actions instead of forced evictions: minimizes customer impact and allows quicker rollback
Burst-governor as shim (not part of core allocator) to reduce blast radius and permit iterative improvement
tasks: P0: implement reconciler loop prototype (Samir) — reads telemetry, writes decision-log
P1: implement Noise Detector Runner rules and test harness (Ava) — spike and ragged-window detectors
P2: build burst-governor shim and integration hooks with runtime token bucket (Eng-Infra)
P3: add console UI for recommendations + approve/reject controls (Frontend)
P4: create chaos experiments and synthetic tenant load generator (SRE)
P5: write unit/e2e tests, add CI gating and canary job for 5 clusters
P6: docs: runbook snippets, playbook sequence, and postmortem references
risks: Oscillation risk if RRO over-corrects; mitigations: hysteresis, cooldown windows, and idempotent decays
False positives flagging legitimate high-traffic customers as noisy — mitigate with confidence thresholds and human-in-loop by default
Telemetry lag causing stale decisions — mitigate with conservative caps and safety bounds
Permissioning mistakes could lead to mis-applied reservations — enforce RBAC and audit logs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal dev): deploy RRO and NDR to staging, run synthetic noisy tenant scenarios for 1 week. Phase 2 (canary): enable read-only recommendations in ops UI for 5 dedicated pools; collect feedback for 72h. Phase 3 (opt-in automation): allow automated 'soft resize' in 3 pilot customers with on-call oversight for first 72h. Phase 4: broader rollout with throttled automation ramp if metrics look stable. Gate criteria: <1% false-positive isolation rate, <2% change in tenant throughput on canaries, no increase in SLO misses.
rollback_plan: All actions are reversible by design. RRO writes candidate deltas to a decision-log and then to staging API; we keep a 1-hour rollback window in automated mode and a 24-hour audit trail for manual reversions. If canary shows regression, flip opt-in flag off and run an automated reversion job that restores prior reservations and clears burst-governor soft limits. Prepare a hotfix path to disable the NDR entirely via feature-flag if unforeseen systemic regressions occur.
metrics_and_dashboards: Grafana: /d/dedicated/reservation-reconciler-summary — reconciliation decisions, applied deltas, confidence scores
Grafana: /d/dedicated/noise-detector-alerts — noisy-tenant events, reason codes, action taken
SLO board: per-tenant 95th latency, eviction rate, token-consumption-rate
PagerDuty: Incident on increased SLO misses tied to automatic actions
